hook_text: Geographers have a saying that sounds wrong: earthquakes don't kill people.
clip_script: So what does? Buildings. When plates get stuck and stress builds up, the rocks finally snap, and seismic waves shake the ground side to side. Standing in an open field, you'd just fall over. But inside a weak brick building, the walls crack, the heavy roof falls, and floors collapse onto each other. Then come the secondary disasters: broken gas pipes start fires, broken water pipes spread disease, and families end up living in tents for months. Under the sea, a big earthquake can lift the ocean itself and send a tsunami racing across at the speed of a jet. In 2004 waves from Indonesia crossed the whole Indian Ocean and even reached South Africa. That's why where you live, and how you build, matters as much as the shaking.
visual_style: A whiteboard ruler bending then snapping into ripples; a person safe in a field versus a cracking brick building; a gas pipe flame; a wave racing across an Indian Ocean map towards Africa.
pacing: Provocative hook, cause and effect chain, a sobering ending.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson and understand earthquakes.
